title: Thompson Sampling for Non-Monotone Convex Ridge Bandits: Monotonicity Is Not Needed for Polynomial Regret
abstract: arXiv:2609.10981v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bakhtiari, Lattimore and Szepesv\'ari (COLT 2025) proved that Thompson sampling (TS) has Bayesian regret $\tilde O(d^{5/2}\sqrt n)$ for bandit convex optimisation with convex \emph{monotone} ridge losses $f(x)=\ell(\ip{x}{\theta})$, and asked whether monotonicity of the link is necessary. We give a qualitative negative answer. For every prior on $[0,1]$-valued, $1$-Lipschitz convex ridge losses with an arbitrary convex, possibly non-monotone, link, and for any fixed measurable selection of minimisers, exact-posterior TS has Bayesian regret $O\big((d+1)^4\sqrt{dn}\,\log(e+nd\max\{1,\diam K\})\big)=\tilde O(d^{9/2}\sqrt n)$. The monotone proof relies on a single-removal John-ellipsoid dichotomy; we show by an explicit twelve-point configuration that this dichotomy fails for non-monotone links, and replace it by an $O(d^2)$ cardinality bound for ``uninformative'' configurations. translated_title: 非单调凸脊赌臂问题的汤普森采样：多项式遗憾并不需要单调性
translated_abstract: Bakhtiari、Lattimore 和 Szepesvári（COLT 2025）证明了汤普森采样（TS）在具有凸*单调*脊损失 $f(x)=\ell(\langle x,\theta\rangle)$ 的赌臂凸优化问题中可取得 $\tilde O(d^{5/2}\sqrt n)$ 的贝叶斯遗憾，并提出了连接函数的单调性是否必要这一开放问题。本文给出了定性上的否定回答。对于取值于 $[0,1]$、1-利普希茨凸脊损失的任意先验分布，连接函数为任意凸函数（可以是非单调的），且对最小值点作任意固定的可测选择时，精确后验 TS 的贝叶斯遗憾为 $O((d+1)^4\sqrt{dn}\,\log(e+nd\max\{1,\operatorname{diam} K\}))=\tilde O(d^{9/2}\sqrt n)$。单调情形的证明依赖于单次移除的 John 椭球二分法；作者通过一个显式的十二点构造表明该二分法在非单调连接函数下失效，并用针对“无信息”构造的 $O(d^2)$ 基数上界来替代之。该上界利用了一个布尔舍入论证：一个 0-1 矩阵……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文证明汤普森采样在连接函数非单调的凸脊赌臂问题上仍能取得 $\tilde O(d^{9/2}\sqrt n)$ 的多项式贝叶斯遗憾，从而以否定方式回答了 COLT 2025 提出的开放问题——连接函数的单调性并非获得多项式遗憾的必要条件。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that Thompson sampling achieves polynomial Bayesian regret $\tilde O(d^{9/2}\sqrt n)$ for convex ridge bandits even with non-monotone links, thereby negatively answering the open question from COLT 2025 of whether monotonicity of the link is necessary for polynomial regret.
